entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Chaldiran, fought on 2 September 1514, was a pivotal event in the Ottoman–Persian Wars, marking a turning point in the conflict between the Safavid Empire and the Ottoman Empire. The battle took place in the mountainous region of Chaldiran, near Lake Urmia in what is now northwestern Iran. The Safavid army, led by Sultan Yahya, suffered a crushing defeat at the hands of the Ottoman forces, led by Sultan Selim I. The loss of Chaldiran led to the displacement of the Safavid court and the eventual capture of Tabriz, a key city in the region. The battle had significant consequences for the region, paving the way for Ottoman expansion into the Middle East.

The Ottoman army, led by Sultan Selim I, made use of their superior artillery and cavalry to devastating effect, routing the Safavid forces. The Safavid army, relying on their traditional tactics of guerrilla warfare, were unable to withstand the Ottoman onslaught. The battle was a decisive victory for the Ottomans, securing control over the region and marking the beginning of a long period of Ottoman expansion.

The Battle of Chaldiran had far-reaching consequences, leading to the displacement of the Safavid court and the eventual capture of Tabriz. The battle marked a significant turning point in the Ottoman–Persian Wars, paving the way for Ottoman expansion into the Middle East. The Safavid Empire, weakened by the loss of Chaldiran, was eventually absorbed into the Ottoman Empire.

In the aftermath of the battle, Sultan Selim I was hailed as a hero, his victory cementing his reputation as a skilled and effective military leader. The battle of Chaldiran remains a pivotal event in the history of the region, a testament to the military prowess of the Ottoman Empire and the enduring legacy of the Safavid Empire.
